title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (May 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-05-25 is the last Tuesday of May 2027. The rule is verified for MAY specifically against three primary-sourced May editions fetched direct 2026-09-06, each read at HTTP 200 and confirmed against its own "Source: May <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and its "Updated:" date rather than trusted by slug: CCI-May-2023 (Updated 2023-05-30, 876,769 bytes), CCI-May-2024 (2024-05-28, 973,591 bytes), CCI-May-2025 (2025-05-27, 343,810 bytes) -- every one the last Tuesday of its May, and ALL THREE double-sourced by the preceding April edition's own next-release line, re-fetched independently this session (CCI-Apr-2023 "The next release is Tuesday, May 30 at 10 AM ET"; CCI-Apr-2024 "Tuesday, May 28th"; CCI-Apr-2025 "Tuesday, May 27th"). CCI-May-2021, CCI-May-2022 and CCI-May-2026 each returned HTTP 200 while serving the current August 2026 edition (332,031 bytes) and are recorded as blocked rather than counted. No May-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a fully double-sourced May record, not a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the consumer-confidence-2027-05-25 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-05-25.from-consumer-confidence-2027-04-27.json, which is now inert. THE CLEAN COUNTERPART to the 04-27 collision print, and the chain's true null control: per the Fed's own posted calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes) 2027 runs April 27-28 then June 8-9, so May 2027 carries NO FOMC meeting at all -- this print sits 27 days after the April decision, 14 days before the June day one, and 4 days before fomc-blackout-start-2027-05-29, with a rule-derived field window of ~05-03 -> 05-17/18 that closes 11-12 days BEFORE that blackout opens. Research finding banked in docs/research/events/consumer-confidence-2027-05-25.md: the May print's real structural feature is not the Fed but MEMORIAL DAY. In 5 of the 6 May prints on the tape (2022-2026) the last Tuesday of May is the session immediately after Memorial Day; 2027 is one of the 15.5% of years (11 of 71, 1990-2060) where Memorial Day falls on May 31 and the print instead precedes it by six days. That composition difference was measured and has NO channel: Tuesday-after-a-Monday-holiday sessions are 0 of 9 against ordinary Tuesdays (n=31 vs 269, smallest p 0.3355) and 0 of 9 against all other sessions. May is also the only month of twelve that is 0 of 9 on BOTH the month-level control (vs the rest of the year, SPY 0.984/0.969, p=0.9445, smallest p across the nine 0.0902 -- 4.6x the next-flattest month) and the position-in-month control (last-5 vs earlier May, 0 of 9), which makes it the calendar's cleanest null and, contra the proposal, the LEAST discriminating site for testing the 03-30 week-level control rule rather than the sharpest. May's own sourced cut-off lags are 8/7/8 days (2023-05-22, 2024-05-21, 2025-05-19), longer than April's 6/6/8, and CCI-May-2025 is the only edition in the chain where the publisher discloses an intra-panel policy split ("About half of the responses were collected after the May 12 announcement of a pause on some tariffs on imports from China"). Estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
